glosses: Mettre dans un travail, une œuvre, de la vivacité, de l'inspiration, du talent, des idées, etc.

examples.text: Canalis ne possède pas le don de vie, il n’insuffle pas l’existence à ses créations.
— Que puis-je pour toi, mon pauvre petit ? Te rendre plus conscient, donc plus malheureux, mais non t’insuffler la volonté que tu n’as pas…

glosses: To cause to become an element of something; to insert or fill.

examples.text: Like every day this hellish summer, someone will come to infuse me with four hours with amphotericin, a weed-killer somewhat effective against cryptococcal meningitis.

glosses: To steep in a liquid, so as to extract the soluble constituents (usually medicinal or herbal).

examples.text:
1806-1831, John Redman Coxe, The American Dispensatory
One scruple of the dried leaves is infused in ten ounces of warm water.

glosses: To inspire; to inspirit or animate; to fill (with).

examples.text: infusing him with self and vain conceit

The uproar of the sea, the yell of the Indians, the rapidity with which the boat at intervals was driven, threatening at every moment to be engulphed, might have infused terror into the most undaunted;[…]

That souls of animals infuse themselves
 Into the trunks of men.
Why should he desire to have qualities infused into his son, which himself never possessed, or knew, or found the want of, in the acquisition of his wealth?
Let it infuse for five minutes.

glosses: To make an infusion with (an ingredient); to tincture; to saturate.
